text:
sam: CI microbench failed for PR #12111 — batch-affinity benchmark shows +12% tail latency (threshold +5%). link: https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/12111
ci-bot: perf-job summary: batch_affinity_microbench: baseline=18.2ms p95 -> PR=20.4ms p95 (+12%). threshold_diff=+7%. logs: /artifacts/12111/perf.log
jordan: ack, can you paste the diff that landed in this PR?
sam: main change was: adjust prefetch window and affinity weight in kernel_selector (commit 9f3a7b2). small batching tweak to prefer affinity 2->3.
april: repro'd locally on my workstation with the microbench harness: `./tools/perf/run_microbench --bench batch_affinity --iters 2000` — saw ~11% tail increase. uploaded flamegraph: https://gist.github.com/april/fg-12111
liam: hmm, I remember 9f3a also nudged the kernel selection scoring to include bandwidth_score. maybe the kernel selector now prefers a kernel with worse memory bandwidth behavior for this seq-len distribution.
mica: note: my trace shows KV cache read hit rate dropped ~6% at the same time window on the CI trace. could be eviction pattern change from prefetch bump.
jordan: sounds like two plausible hypotheses: (A) kernel selector mispredicted and chose a suboptimal kernel, (B) prefetch/affinity change caused KV thrash and killed latency. we should bisect.
sam: proposed plan: 1) run quick git-bisect on CI to identify culprit commit range, 2) if kernel-selector commit is culprit, revert the scoring tweak; if prefetch is culprit revert prefetch. tagging this PR as rollout-blocker for now :warning:
sam: bisect command I plan to run: `git bisect start HEAD v2026-03-01 -- scripts/ci/run_batch_affinity_bench.sh`
jordan: I'll kick off the bisect on a CI worker and stream logs here. starting now.
ci-bot: bisect-run 3512347890 started. running jobs 1/40. will post updates as jobs finish.
april: attaching snapshot of hotspot from my local profile: top functions: `kernel_selector::score_candidates`, `kv_cache::evict_if_needed`, `batcher::build_batch_prefer_affinity`. the kernel_selector path shows increased time inside mem-bound heuristics.
liam: to add: try forcing kernel override on a candidate to see perf: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fast_gemm ./tools/perf/run_microbench ...` — if that regresses less, it's kernel choice.
mica: also recommend rerunning microbench with KV cache warmup flag `--kv-warmup=1000` to see if hit rate restores and latency improves.
jordan: CI bisect update: narrowed to commits [9f3a7b2..c4d9e11]. 8 commits left. next batches in ~25m.
sam: if the bisect shows the kernel selector commit as bad, I'll open an immediate revert PR for that scoring change.
ci-bot: bisect-run 3512347890 update: job 12/40 failed threshold at job 12: candidate commit c4d9e11.
jordan: that points to commit c4d9e11 — which is the affinity/batch packing change. grabbing the diff.
april: interesting, c4d9e11 changes batch packing to bias groups by affinity and also increases default prefetch_len from 64->96. both could affect memory bw.
liam: okay, plan: run two confirmatory CI jobs, one with prefetch_len reverted, one with packing reverted. if prefetch revert fixes it -> revert prefetch change.
sam: launching confirm jobs. also adding `rollout-blocker` label on the PR and pausing merges to the runtime branch. @eng-sre please hold the next merge window.
mica: I'll prepare a short perf regression note for the release notes and link the flamegraphs.
jordan: confirm-run results: revert-prefetch job: p95 back to baseline (18.3ms). revert-packing job: p95 still +9%. looks like prefetch_len increase is the culprit.
sam: thanks all — reverting the prefetch change in a hotfix PR now. assigning to @liam for review.
liam: on it, will push the revert and include a test to lock prefetch_len in microbench config.
april: will update eval harness to include a kv-warmup variant so we catch this pattern in future.
ci-bot: hotfix PR 12112 created to revert commit c4d9e11 (prebump prefetch_len). status: pending CI.
sam: marking thread resolved once hotfix CI passes. great debugging run, team :thumbsup:
